prompt: THE rule your writings break most: when two verbs meet…
options: only the FIRST is conjugated — the second stays infinitive: je veux mangER
explain: One conjugated verb per clause. Everything after it stays in the dictionary form — no matter how far from the pronoun it sits. (This answers your note on Sprint 8/8: distance doesn't matter; following another verb does.)

prompt: “je suis veux un gâteau” is wrong because…
options: suis and veux are BOTH conjugated — pick one: je veux un gâteau
explain: English “I am wanting” tempts you to add suis. French never stacks two conjugated verbs.

prompt: Say: “I want to close the door.” (fermer = to close)
hint: veux is conjugated → fermer stays infinitive, no “de”, no “fermé”.
explain: je veux fermer la porte — your past slips: “je veux fermé” and “je voudrais de fermer”.

prompt: Say: “I would like to speak French.”
explain: je voudrais parler — verb + infinitive, glued directly.

prompt: Say: “I'm not going to speak with you.” (informal)
answer: je ne vais pas parler avec toi
je vais pas parler avec toi
hint: ne…pas wraps vais. Then parler directly — no “pour”.
explain: je ne vais pas parler avec toi — this morning you wrote “pas pour parler”. pour = in order to; it doesn't belong between aller and its verb.

options: de — ce n'est pas possible DE voler
explain: possible de + infinitive. Your “possible pour voler” → possible de voler. (pour + verb = “in order to”.)

prompt: Say: “It's not possible to fly today.” (voler = to fly)
answer: ce n'est pas possible de voler aujourd'hui
explain: ce n'est pas possible de voler aujourd'hui.

prompt: Say: “I'm going to sleep.” (dormir = to sleep)
hint: aller + infinitive = near future. Nothing in between.
explain: je vais dormir — clean, like your best sentence this week.
